question: How many casual leaves do I get in a year?
answer: 8 days.  You’re credited with 8 CL days each year on 1 January, and any unused CL lapses on 31 December. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 4).

question: How many sick leaves are there?
answer: 8 days. Sick Leave entitlement is 8 days per year, credited on 1 January and lapses on 31 December. (Source: HR‑02 Leave Policy, Section 4)

question: How does earned leave accrue?
answer: Earned leave accrues at **1.5 days per month** (18 days a year), credited at the end of each month. For new joiners, accrual starts in the month of joining if the date is on or before the 15th, otherwise from the following month. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 7)

question: What is the EL carry-forward limit?
answer: 30 days – You may carry forward up to 30 days of EL; anything above that lapses at year‑end. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 7)

question: Can I encash my leave?
answer: Yes, you can encash up to 30 days of earned leave when you leave the company. This applies only to Earned Leave (EL) and is permitted on separation (not while in service). (Source: HR-13 HR Quick FAQ, Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 7.3)

question: When do I need a medical certificate?
answer: Yes – you need a medical certificate if you take more than 2 consecutive days of sick leave (including weekends and holidays).   | (Reference: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 6).

question: How long is maternity leave?
answer: 26 weeks for the first two children, 12 weeks from the third child onward.   | This is the statutory maternity leave length outlined in the company’s leave policy.   | (Sources: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 8; HR-13 HR Quick FAQ, Section Leave and Holidays)

question: How much paternity leave do I get?
answer: 10 working days.   | This is paid paternity leave for male employees, must be taken within 6 months of birth and can be split into 2 blocks.   |  | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 9)

question: Bereavement leave if my grandmother passes away?
answer: 2 days   | Because a grandparent’s death entitles you to 2 working days of bereavement leave.   |  | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 10)

question: How much marriage leave do I get?
answer: 5 working days of paid leave, available once during your service and to be applied for at least 15 days in advance; you must take it within 3 months before or after the wedding date. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 11)

question: How many public holidays are there?
answer: 12 public holidays, as stated in the leave policy. This is a fixed number each year with no replacement if a holiday falls on a weekend (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 13).

question: Is Diwali a holiday this year?
answer: Yes – Diwali is a company holiday on 9 November 2026, Monday.   | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section: Annexure A)

question: Is Independence Day a holiday? Is it replaced?
answer: Yes. Independence Day (15 Aug 2026) is listed as a public holiday and, because it falls on a Saturday, it is not replaced. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 13)

question: How much notice do I need for 5 days of earned leave?
answer: 7 working days notice. For 4–10 days of earned leave, you must give 7 days advance notice and get your reporting manager’s approval. (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 7)

question: I take CL on Friday and Monday. How many days are deducted?
answer: 4 days. The weekend between Friday and Monday counts as CL under the sandwich rule. |  | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section: Annexure B)

question: And if I take EL on Friday and Monday?
answer: 2 days.   | The sandwich rule does not apply to earned leave, so each day (Friday and Monday) counts separately.   | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section: Annexure B)

question: How long is comp-off valid?
answer: 60 days   | Comp-off must be taken within 60 days of being earned; after that it lapses.   | (Source: HR-02 Leave Policy, Section 12)

question: I joined on 10 June. How much CL do I get this year?
answer: 4.5 days of CL. It’s calculated pro‑rata from when you joined—June is counted because you started before the 15th—so 7 months × 8 CL days ÷ 12 = 4.67, rounded to 4.5. (Source: HR‑02 Leave Policy, Section: Annexure B)

question: What are the office timings and core hours?
answer: Office timings: log in between 8:30 AM and 10:30 AM, then work a 9‑hour day that includes a 1‑hour break (so the day ends 9 hours after you log in).   | Core hours: 10:30 AM to 4:30 PM, when everyone must be available for meetings and collaboration.   | (See HR-13 HR Quick FAQ and HR‑03 Attendance, Working Hours and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 2.)

question: How many days must I come to office?
answer: 3 days a week (at least 2 on anchor days: Tues‑Wed‑Thu). Probationary staff must be in the office 4 days a week for the first 3 months unless the manager approves otherwise. (Source: HR‑13 HR Quick FAQ, Section Attendance and Work Model; HR‑03 Attendance, Working Hours and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 7)

question: How many extra WFH days can I take?
answer: 12 days a year, plus up to 10 days a year from another city with approval.   | You can take 12 extra work‑from‑home days each year, and if you want to work from a different city you may take up to an additional 10 days with approval.   | (Source: HR-13 HR Quick FAQ, Section: Attendance and Work Model)

question: What happens if I log in late?
answer: Late login is recorded as a late mark. On the 3rd late mark in a month, a half‑day of Casual Leave is deducted (or another leave type if CL is unavailable). (Up to 2 late marks per month have no impact.) (Source: HR-03 Attendance, Working Hours and Hybrid Work Policy, Section 5)

question: When is salary credited?
answer: Last working day of the month; salary is credited automatically into your registered bank account.   | (Source: HR-06 Compensation, Payroll and Benefits Policy, Section 3)

question: What is the reimbursement cut-off date?
answer: 22nd of the month.   | Reimbursement claims must be submitted through the portal on or before the 22nd; later claims are paid in the next month.   | (Source: HR-06 Compensation, Payroll and Benefits Policy, Section 3 and 8)

question: What does health insurance cover?
answer: Rs. 5 ,00 000 per family per year for you, your spouse and up to two children, starting on the date of joining. Parents can be added at group rates. (Source: HR-13 HR Quick FAQ, Section Pay and Benefits; HR-06 Compensation, Payroll and Benefits Policy, Section 7.1)

question: When am I eligible for gratuity?
answer: 5 years of continuous service. |  | (After 5 years of continuous service, you are eligible for gratuity. Source: HR‑13 HR Quick FAQ)

question: What is the referral bonus for a B3 hire?
answer: Rs. 20,000. B3 is in the B1‑B4 range, so the referral bonus is Rs. 20,000, paid after the referred person completes 6 months of service.   | (Source: HR-06 Compensation, Payroll and Benefits Policy, Section 7.6)

question: How long is probation?
answer: 6 months, extendable once for up to 3 months.   | This is the standard probation period for new permanent employees, and it can be extended for a maximum of three additional months if needed.   | (Source: HR-13 HR Quick FAQ, Section: Joining, Performance and Exit; HR-07 Recruitment, Onboarding and Probation Policy, Section 7)

question: What is my notice period as a confirmed B4 employee?
answer: 60 days. As a confirmed employee in bands B1‑B4, the policy states the notice period is 60 days. (Source: HR-11 Separation and Exit Policy, Section 3)

question: When do I get full and final settlement?
answer: Within 45 days of your last working day.   | This is required by the Separation and Exit Policy. (Source: HR-11 Separation and Exit Policy, Section 5)
